derived_from.aggregation: The design point's devices are collapsed into ONE logical device holding their aggregate resource.  Both anchor points have token_slots = 1, so four of the five analytical terms are unchanged by the collapse; the fifth, link_latency, is removed by it and is reported as a structural residual.

description: N5 design-target machine for the HBM role of the analytical anchor pair Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 vs Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (Qwen3-8B, batch 1, context 8192).  DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: every parameter here is an analytical value divided by a stated denominator or an explicit statement that the analytical model prices no counterpart, and every entry carries its derivation in `note` and its technology.json grade in `analytical_grade`.  Nothing in this file is characterized; the measured SKY130 and ASAP7 tables are untouched and describe a different machine.  Generated by tools/derive_cycle_machine.py from results/roofline/n5_vs_b200/analytical.json; run that tool with --check to verify this file still matches the anchor it claims.

clock.frequency_hz.note: 3 sequencer cycles (sequencer.fetch_cycles + decode_cycles + issue_cycles, the cycle model's per-instruction front end) divided by technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s.  The analytical model states no clock; this is the one analytical quantity that fixes one.  Every rate below is an analytical B/s or ops/s divided by this clock, so a different clock would move the per-cycle numbers and leave every derived TIME unchanged.

engine.attention.bytes_per_cycle.note: The analytical model prices no engine byte-port bandwidth.  Both machines are given the larger of the pair's weight-path rates (4.752960e+14 B/s) so that no simulated time is attributed to an engine port the analytical model does not model.  At the shipped 64 B/cycle this would throttle DMA to 6.400e+10 B/s, 7426x below the ROM array it drains.

engine.attention.fixed_latency_cycles.note: technology.json#latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s 3.2e-08 s + one global wire traversal sqrt(reticle.area_mm2) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm = 4.282231e-09 s, the analytical array-pass boundary 3.628223e-08 s, times the clock = 36.2822 cycles.  The analytical model charges 4 of these per layer; the cycle model charges one per engine instruction and has no per-layer hook, so the difference between the deployment's instructions per layer and 4 is a reported residual, not a tuned parameter.

engine.attention.lanes.default.note: Same as engine.tensor.lanes.default.  The analytical model prices all arithmetic at one roof and names no engine families, so every family is given the same width and the same per-lane depth.  For 'attention' the cycle model divides tile work by lanes x work_per_lane_cycle directly, so the product is the whole story.

engine.attention.minimum_cycles.note: The schema minimum.  The analytical model prices no per-instruction floor, so the derived machine imposes the smallest one the cycle model permits.

engine.attention.queue_depth.default.note: Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent descriptor count.  The analytical model prices no queue occupancy.

engine.attention.queues.default.note: Submission queues, shared by both machines by construction. engine.tensor.lanes.default.note: The narrowest tensor operator output width in Qwen3-8B (1024: the GQA key and value projections, num_key_value_heads x head_dim).  At batch 1 the cycle model's tensor rate is min(lanes, tile_cols*issue_window, cols) x work_per_lane_cycle x clock, so lanes above the operator's own output width are masked and deliver nothing.  1024 is the largest lane count for which EVERY tensor operator of this model runs at the full derived roof; at 4096 the achieved rate falls to 88.5% of the roof and at 12288 to 42.6%.  The pair (lanes, work_per_lane_cycle) is a gauge split of one analytical quantity -- their product times the clock is what the design point pins -- and this rule fixes the split by exactness.

engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.note: compute roof / (lanes x clock), in work-counter units.  The roof is area_fractions.compute 0.22290895663237373 x silicon_area_mm2 3260.0 x technology_derivations.compute_ops_s_per_mm2.bf16 679903147699.7579 x efficiencies.compute 0.55 = 2.7174080677e+14 ops/s.  Verified against the artifact: 15136811008 ops / that roof = 5.570312088214652e-05 s, which reproduces the published component_times_s.compute 5.570312088214652e-05 EXACTLY, to the last bit in double precision.  Units: the cost table declares this parameter in work/lane/cycle and the shipped characterized value was measured as (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) / cycles; the analytical operations count is multiplies AND adds too (operations_per_active_parameter = 2), so no conversion is needed and none is applied.  That makes the machine's MAC rate lanes x work_per_lane_cycle / 2 x clock = 1.3587040338e+14 MAC/s.  In the cycle model this value divides the K extent (ceil(tile_depth x work_scale / work_per_lane_cycle)), so it is the reduction-tree width of one output lane -- 132.69 MACs deep -- and not a second lane count.

hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.note: One HBM3E channel.  points[ROM] serves KV from 20 stacks at 1.800000e+13 B/s and points[GPU] serves weights and KV from 16 stacks at 1.440000e+13 B/s; at 8 channels per stack both give 112.5 B/cycle at this clock.  The two design points buy different numbers of the SAME channel, which is why hbm.channels is the only HBM parameter the two machines are permitted to differ on.

hbm.channels.default.note: 16 HBM3E stacks x 8 channels: 2 B200 packages of 8 stacks, serving weights AND KV from one pool (overlap_rule 'weights and KV share one memory system: their times add') at points[GPU].peak_weight_read_bytes_s 1.440000e+13 B/s.

hbm.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the HBM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across channels.

hbm.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  KV lives in HBM on both sides of this anchor, so that primitive is the HBM access latency.

hbm.transaction_bytes.note: 225 B = 2 x hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel, the smallest integer burst for which the cycle model's ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle) is exact and no channel bandwidth is lost to quantisation.  The analytical model has no burst-size concept.

hbm.write_latency_cycles.note: The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  KV lives in HBM on both sides of this anchor, so that primitive is the HBM access latency.

model.max_modeled_transactions_per_acces.note: A simulator fidelity knob, not a machine parameter; carried unchanged.  Above it an access reserves per-unit time in bulk, which keeps total occupancy exact and only coarsens the interleave.

queue.transit_cycles.note: Not priced by the analytical model.  Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent cycle count; the run's issue_cycles, queue_stall_cycles and wait_stall_cycles counters report its contribution separately, so it is attributed rather than zeroed.

rom.arrays.default.note: The GPU design point 'Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor' has no ROM (area_fractions.rom = 0.0).  These four rom.* values exist because the cost-table schema requires the full parameter set; no MEMORY_OBJECT in the HBM deployment is stamped StorageClass.ROM, so the ROM unit pool is never scheduled.

rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array.note: Inert: the GPU design point has no ROM.  See rom.arrays.default.

rom.interleave_bytes.note: Inert: the GPU design point has no ROM.  See rom.arrays.default.

rom.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical model prices no ROM access latency.  The ROM array is on die, so the one analytical latency primitive that applies is a global wire traversal of the reticle: sqrt(reticle.area_mm2 815.0) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm 1.5e-10 = 4.282231e-09 s = 4.2822 cycles.

rom.transaction_bytes.note: Inert: the GPU design point has no ROM.  See rom.arrays.default.

Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent cycle count; the run's issue_cycles, queue_stall_cycles and wait_stall_cycles counters report its contribution separately, so it is attributed rather than zeroed.

sequencer.decode_cycles.note: The cycle model's instruction decode.  These three are the machine's per-instruction front end and their sum is what technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s prices; that identity is what fixes clock.frequency_hz, so they cannot be changed without changing the clock.

sram.banks.default.note: 32 banks, the bank count both shipped Qwen capabilities already declare, kept so the compiled bank masks mean what they meant before.  The design points allocate no SRAM area at all (area_fractions.sram = 0.0), so no analytical value fixes this.

sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.note: The analytical design point prices NO SRAM term and allocates no SRAM area, so there is nothing to reproduce.  banks x ports x this rate x clock = 5.242880e+14 B/s, which exceeds the larger of the two weight paths (4.753021e+14 B/s) so that the activation store cannot bind and no simulated time is attributed to a store the analytical model does not price.  This is a deliberate neutralisation for a validation experiment: the derived machine is NOT a complete machine and its absolute tokens/s is an upper bound.

sram.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port so the model's ceil() is exact.  See that parameter.

sram.ports_per_bank.default.note: Chosen with sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port so that the activation store cannot be the binding term.  See that parameter.

sram.transaction_bytes.note: Set equal to sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port so the model's ceil() is exact.  See that parameter.

state.backing_storage_class.note: STATE objects are timed as if they lived in SRAM, unchanged from the shipped tables.  ADR-003 does not bind the placement of a state resource and the analytical model has no state term.
